transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Um, hi. I guess… work is kind of the main reason. I keep getting up from my station when I’m supposed to stay there, or I’ll pop up during meetings before I even realize I’m doing it. I don’t mean to cause trouble or anything, but my supervisor said it’s turning into a safety issue because I sort of just take off without thinking. I’m not trying to be difficult, I just… I guess I need help figuring out why I can’t stay put like I’m supposed to.
Did you have this same kind of trouble sitting still when you were a child?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I wasn’t trying to be bad or anything, but even in elementary school I had a hard time staying in my seat. I’d talk over the teacher sometimes, or blurt stuff out before I was supposed to. I remember getting notes sent home for wandering around the classroom too. It’s kind of embarrassing to say, but yeah, it was there when I was little.
Do you often have trouble staying focused on tasks?

Yeah… I mean, I try to. Like with inventory logs at work, or when I’m reading the CNC training pages, I’ll start out really meaning to pay attention. But after a few minutes it’s like the numbers or the words kind of blur together, and then I realize I didn’t actually take any of it in. So I have to go back and reread it or redo the log. I don’t know if that counts, but it happens a lot.
Have you ever had a period where you needed much less sleep than usual and still felt full of energy?
Um… I don’t think so? Like, I have nights where I don’t sleep great, but I wouldn’t say I felt totally energized after or anything. I’m usually tired if I don’t sleep. Is that what you mean?
Do these same problems happen outside of work too, like at home or in other parts of your life?

Um… I guess I haven’t really kept track of it that way. At home I can get kind of restless, but I don’t know if it’s the same as work or if I’m just tired after my shift. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is. Maybe it happens some, but I’m not totally sure what would count.
At home, do you also have trouble staying seated when you mean to?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I try to stay put, especially if we’re having a meeting or I’m supposed to be at my station, but I’ll just kind of pop up or walk off before I really think about it. I don’t mean to be difficult.

That’s actually part of why I came in… my supervisor said it’s turning into a safety issue at work because I leave my station when I’m supposed to stay there. At home it’s maybe not as obvious, but the “not staying seated” thing is definitely something I struggle with.
Do you often have a hard time waiting your turn?

Um… I’m not totally sure. I mean, I don’t love waiting, but I don’t know if it’s more than normal. Like, I try not to cut in or anything. Are you asking about lines, or like when someone else is talking?
Do you often interrupt other people before they finish talking?

Yeah… I think I do that. I don’t mean it in a rude way, but I’ll kind of jump in before someone’s done, like at work if the lead is asking something I’ll answer before they finish, or I’ll cut into coworkers talking. I usually realize after because people get irritated, and then I feel bad. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you often lose things you need for work or daily activities, like tools, keys, paperwork, or your phone?

Um… I don’t think that’s a big one for me? I mean, I misplace stuff sometimes like anyone does, but I wouldn’t say I’m always losing my phone or tools or anything. At work I try pretty hard to keep things where they’re supposed to be.

Is that okay—like, if it happens once in a while, is that what you mean, or more like all the time?
